lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Riverside Cinema | Box Office Attendant | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Sold tickets and concessions during evening shifts and balanced the cash drawer at close.
- Trained 3 new attendants on the ticketing system and the refund policy.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed.
items.because: They aren’t relevant to qualifications and can introduce avoidable bias.

items.says: Check that “B.S. in Statistics” is the university’s official degree title.
items.because: The line should use the exact form.

items.says: The bullet mostly lists duties; consider adding a meaningful measure of volume, accuracy, or customer-service responsibility.
items.because: It would make the cinema role more useful for analyst applications.

items.says: Clarify what “2.4M customers” refers to.
Specify the period or population used for the retention measure.
Make clear that 22% to 27% is a 5-percentage-point change.
items.because: It could be mistaken for a 5% relative increase.

items.says: Be precise about how directly the dashboard contributed to the result.
Clarify whether “3 days” means working time or elapsed time.
items.because: The comparison with 2 hours is otherwise ambiguous.

items.says: The join direction appears wrong for finding customers with no orders.
items.because: The query generally needs to preserve customer records.

items.says: Checking for a null customer name appears wrong for this task.
items.because: A null customer name can occur for other reasons; the missing value should be checked on the orders side.

items.says: Add a concrete result of the finding if available.
items.because: The bullet describes a method but not what the finding enabled.

items.says: The opening gerund phrase has a grammar problem.
items.because: The comma separates the described work from its verb.

items.says: Make the contribution and outcome easier to follow.
items.because: The bullet packs several substantial tasks together.

items.says: Confirm that “dbt-style SQL models” accurately describes the implementation.
items.because: It could imply that you used dbt if you did not.

items.says: Clarify what the change from 58% to 81% measures and over what period.
Identify the type of recommendations or their eventual impact if possible.
State the period or baseline behind “halving.”
items.because: It may not be clear to a reader.

items.says: Checking p-values daily and stopping at the first one below 0.05 is statistically invalid without an appropriate sequential-testing method.
items.because: Repeated checking and stopping increases the false-positive risk.

items.says: Clarify the period over which hold time was measured.
Clarify your role in the staffing change.
items.because: The wording could imply you made the operational decision if you only recommended it.

items.says: “Writes” has the wrong tense.
items.because: The role ended in 2022 and the surrounding bullets use past tense.

items.says: Give a clear measurement period or basis for “cut query errors … by half.”
Separate the fraud-extract automation from unrelated duties if retaining them.
items.because: The overloaded bullet obscures the strongest result.

items.says: Clarify what saved the fraud team 10 hours a month and what that figure measures.
items.because: The final clause makes the source of the saving unclear.

items.says: Keep the ongoing date current and confirm that the project is still active.
items.because: It is marked as ongoing.

items.says: Consider adding a code or portfolio link.
items.because: It could help readers assess the work.

items.says: Clarify and accurately label “within 12% mean absolute error.”
items.because: Mean absolute error is normally expressed in the units of the predicted quantity.

items.says: Clarify the forecasting grain and how the model was validated.
items.because: Readers need to know especially how you avoided using future information.

items.says: The claimed 50% reduction is incorrect.
items.because: Going from 300 to 200 hours is a reduction of 100 hours, or one-third.

items.says: Make clear that the reduction occurred in a replay or simulation.
items.because: It was not a real-world reduction.

items.says: Explain the comparison baseline or assumptions if space allows.
The change from 60% to 75% is misstated as a 15% increase.
items.because: It is a 15-percentage-point increase, not a 15% relative increase.

items.says: Define a forecast “hit” and explain how it was evaluated.
Ensure the hit-rate and forecasting bullets describe distinct aspects of the work.
items.because: Otherwise they may repeat the same result.

items.says: Add the measurement period or basis for the wait-time figures.
items.because: It may not be obvious.

items.says: Clarify how repeat-visitor records were matched, if relevant.
items.because: “Matched repeat visitors” could prompt questions about the process.

items.says: Clarify how personal or sensitive information was handled, if relevant.
Quantify the unique-household result if possible.
items.because: That would make the result stronger.

items.says: List other tools you actually used, if relevant.
items.because: The experience suggests a BI platform, version control, or a transformation tool may be worth listing.

items.says: Reconsider listing “dashboards” as a method.
items.because: It is more of an output than a method.

items.says: Make the other methods more specific.
items.because: The terms are broad.

items.says: Keep the cinema role concise.
items.because: The analyst experience is the main story, and the cinema role should not compete with it.
